title: Planning-node lookup lives in the template module
description:
Move the pure lookup that finds a container's bracket planning node, and the container-label interpolation it depends on, out of `commands` into `crate::templates`, so the validation layer stops importing it from `commands`.

## Background

- `find_planning_node` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:2284-2309`), `PLAN_DOC_LABEL` (`:2323`) and `planning_node_plan_path` (`:2332-2338`) are pure functions over issues and a `GraphTemplate`. `commands/mod.rs:96` re-exports the two functions for `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:682-683`, an inverted dependency from the validation layer onto `commands`.
- `find_planning_node` calls `declared_container_label` (`crates/jit/src/commands/template_expand.rs:626-653`, `pub(super)`), which interpolates container tokens through `InterpolationContext` (`template_expand.rs:528-610`). Template application also uses both (`commands/template.rs:14-15,916`; the `template_expand.rs` tests at `:1221-1303`).
- `crate::templates` (`crates/jit/src/templates.rs`) already owns `GraphTemplate` (`:279`), `RoleBindings` (`:226`) and `GraphTemplate::plan_doc_location` (`:511`), and imports nothing from `commands`.
- Callers: `commands/validate.rs:967-968` (`plan_document_paths`), `:1042-1043` (`plan_content_with_issues`), `validation/repository.rs:682-683` (`project_plan_content`), `commands/template.rs:916`, and the unit test `test_find_planning_node_resolves_template_declared_container_label` (`commands/validate.rs:2541`).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `find_planning_node`, `planning_node_plan_path`, the plan-document label and `declared_container_label`, with the container-token interpolation they use, are defined under `crate::templates`; `commands` defines and re-exports none of them.
- [hard] REQ-02: `crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs` resolves planning nodes through `crate::templates`, and no production code under `crates/jit/src/validation/` names a `crate::commands` item for it.
- [hard] REQ-03: Template application and validation resolve the same planning node and container label as before: the moved unit test passes in the templates module, and the template-application and scope-validation suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Planning-node and container-label resolution move from commands into crate::templates.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One pure lookup moves between modules with its import sites and one test.

title: One resolver for plan-document references
description:
Resolve a breakable container's plan document in one function and make every site that needs it call that function.

## Background

The chain breakable type → container template with a plan-document location → planning node → planning node's `plan`-labelled document reference is written three times:

- `plan_document_paths` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:949-972`) derives the paths a validation capture must read;
- `plan_content_with_issues` (`commands/validate.rs:1008-1055`) reads the content for graph-rule evaluation, and serves mutation callers too (`commands/mod.rs:2686,3176`, `commands/dependency.rs:403`, `commands/bulk_update.rs:377`, and `commands/issue.rs:90` through `plan_content_from_image`);
- `project_plan_content` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:657-695`) reads the content inside repository validation.

The two content readers share one rule: an absent plan whose planning node is not `done` is omitted, and an absent plan whose planning node is `done` is an error. The scope-validation tests over external plans (`crates/jit/tests/cli_query_graph/scope_validation_tests.rs:909-1085,1196,1221`) exercise the rule end to end.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One pure function in `crate::templates` maps a container, the issues by id and the template registry to the container's plan-document reference, or none, together with whether its planning node is `done`.
- [hard] REQ-02: `plan_document_paths`, `plan_content_with_issues` and `project_plan_content` obtain plan-document references only through that function; no other code walks from a breakable type to a planning node's plan document.
- [hard] REQ-03: One templates unit test owns the resolution cases: an inline plan (no reference), a relinked non-default path, and the not-done and done planning node; the scope-validation suite passes unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Capture discovery, plan-content projection and repository validation resolve plan documents through one function.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three copies of one resolution collapse into one pure function in one focused change.

title: Configuration accessors for content format and strictness
description:
Give `JitConfig` one accessor for the repository's default content format and one for its validation strictness, each applying the default when `[validation]` or the key is absent, and move the validation layer and projection rendering onto them.

## Background

- `[validation].content_format` and `[validation].strictness` are typed at load: absent means Markdown and loose respectively (`crates/jit/src/config.rs`, `ValidationConfig`).
- Callers restate the default when `config.validation` is `None`. In the validation layer and repository state: `collect_rule_findings` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:561-566`), `collect_item_link_findings` (`validation/repository.rs:707-712`), and `repo_content_format` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/projection_render.rs:245-260`, called at `:102`), which also re-implements the token match with its own error.
- Command-layer readers move separately, onto these accessors.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `JitConfig::content_format()` returns the repository's content format, Markdown when undeclared, and `JitConfig::strictness()` returns its strictness, loose when undeclared; each default is stated once, in its accessor.
- [hard] REQ-02: The three listed readers read the content format through `JitConfig::content_format()`, and `projection_render.rs` keeps no token matching or default of its own.
- [hard] REQ-03: Config unit tests show both accessors' result for an absent `[validation]` table, an absent key and a declared value.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged; the projection error variant for an invalid format goes away because loading rejects such a value.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: JitConfig states the content-format and strictness defaults once, and the validation layer reads them there.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Two accessors and the three non-command readers fit one small change.

title: Commands read content format and strictness through the configuration accessors
description:

- `CommandExecutor::repo_content_format` (`commands/mod.rs:2634-2641`), called from `commands/validate.rs:1516,1617,1784,1943`, `commands/bulk_update.rs:624` and `commands/item.rs:135,287,365`.

title: Built-in validation pass names are one validation-layer vocabulary
description:
Declare the rule names of the built-in validation passes as one closed vocabulary in the validation layer, so `crates/jit/src/validation/` no longer imports them from `commands`.

## Background

- `DANGLING_LINK_RULE`, `ENFORCEMENT_DRIFT_RULE` and `REVIEW_PLACEHOLDER_RULE` are `&str` constants in `crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:12,19,23`, re-exported at `commands/mod.rs:97`. Repository validation reads them from `commands` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:622,646,769,832`), and spells the fourth built-in name, `rules-file`, as a literal (`:215`). `commands/validate.rs:1609` spells it again.
- Other readers: `commands/validate.rs` (dangling, drift and placeholder passes), `commands/gate_check.rs:508,587,592` and tests (`validation/repository.rs:1006,1236,1263`, `commands/gate_check.rs:2898,3038`, `crates/jit/tests/cli_item_validate/item_cli_tests.rs`, `cli_item_validate/validate_cli_rule_tests.rs`, `cli_repo_workflow/profile_acceptance_tests.rs`).
- Closed vocabularies are declared through the crate's wire-vocabulary macro (`domain/vocabulary.rs`), which emits `as_str`, `ALL`, `FromStr` and serde from one list.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A `BuiltInPass` vocabulary in the validation layer, declared through the wire-vocabulary macro, names `rules-file`, `dangling-item-link`, `enforcement-drift` and `review-placeholder`, and every built-in finding takes its rule name from it.
- [hard] REQ-02: The three `commands` constants and their re-export no longer exist, and no code spells a built-in pass name as a string literal outside the vocabulary declaration and tests that assert wire output.
- [hard] REQ-03: Findings keep their wire rule names: the existing validation and gate suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: The built-in pass rule names become a closed vocabulary in the validation layer.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One closed vocabulary replaces three constants and one literal at a known set of sites.

title: Local rules compile each schema once per evaluation set
description:
Compile the local rules' JSON Schemas once and reuse them across issues, so whole-repository validation stops recompiling every schema for every issue.

## Background

- `evaluate_local` (`crates/jit/src/validation/local.rs`) desugars each matching rule's schema (`:302-305`) and builds a new `SchemaEngine` per call (`:316-317`). The engine caches compiled validators by schema key (`crates/jit/src/validation/engine.rs:177-183,408-440`), but the cache lives only for that one call.
- Repository validation calls `evaluate_local` once per issue (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:568-576`), so each schema compiles once per issue.
- Single-issue write paths also call `evaluate_local` (`commands/mod.rs`, `commands/template.rs`, `commands/bulk_update.rs`, `commands/gate_check.rs`, `commands/validate.rs`) and its tests (`validation/local.rs`, `repository_state/default_rules.rs`, `tests/fast_docs_templates/content_format_dispatch.rs`, `tests/fast_rules/example_rulesets_tests.rs`, `tests/fast_rules/default_rules_registry_derivation_tests.rs`). `SchemaEngine` is `!Sync`, which suits a single-threaded report.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A compiled local-rule set holds the desugared schemas and one `SchemaEngine`, and evaluates any number of issues; each distinct schema compiles at most once per set.
- [hard] REQ-02: `evaluate_local` keeps its signature and builds a compiled set for its one issue, so its callers are unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: Repository validation evaluates every issue through one compiled set per validation.
- [hard] REQ-04: A unit test evaluates two issues against one compiled set and shows that both use the same compiled validator for a shared schema.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Repository validation evaluates its issues through one compiled local-rule set, compiling each schema once.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One compiled-rules type in local.rs plus its one repository-validation consumer.

title: Graph findings record their firing subject
description:
Record on every graph finding the issue whose rule application fired it, so a selection can tell the firing subject apart from the issue the finding is attributed to.

## Background

- `GraphFinding` (`crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:262-307`) carries `issue_id` (attribution) and a private config-error flag. Constructors: `for_issue` (`:277`), `unattributed` (`:289`), `issue_finding` (`:742`) and `config_error` (`:753`); `evaluate_one` (`:600-690`) dispatches the assertion kinds.
- Attribution and subject differ in two cases: a `label-coverage` finding with `container-from-label` is attributed to the resolved container while the breakdown issue fired it (`:960-1060`), and a pointer that resolves to no issue or to several is a configuration error with no attribution although one issue fired it (`resolve_container` call sites in the same range).
- `label-uniqueness` findings (`:692-731`) and rule-level configuration errors have no firing subject.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `GraphFinding` exposes `subject: Option<IssueId>`: the firing issue for every finding produced while applying a rule to one issue, configuration errors raised for one firing issue included, and `None` for `label-uniqueness` findings and rule-level configuration errors.
- [hard] REQ-02: Graph unit tests show a `container-from-label` coverage finding attributed to the container with the breakdown issue as subject, an unresolvable pointer reported as a configuration error whose subject is the firing issue, and a `label-uniqueness` finding with no subject.
- [hard] REQ-03: Attribution, messages and severities are unchanged, and the existing graph and validation suites pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Each graph finding records the issue whose rule application produced it, separately from its attribution.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One field set by the existing finding constructors inside graph.rs.

title: Container pointers resolve through an index built once per graph evaluation
description:
Resolve `container-from-label` pointers against an issue-id index built once per graph evaluation, removing the per-pointer scan that dominates validation time.

## Background

- `resolve_container` (`crates/jit/src/validation/graph.rs:1306-1316`) parses the pointer as an `IssueIdPrefix` and tests it against every issue with `IssueIdPrefix::matches`, which normalises (allocates a lowercase, hyphen-free copy of) each candidate id. It runs once per pointer label, from `evaluate_label_coverage` (`:960-1060`) and `graph_rule_plan_source_ids` (`:501-525`), so resolution is O(labels × issues) allocations.
- A release-build profile of `jit validate` on this repository attributes about 29% of inclusive time to that normalisation (`dev/active/9876a23a-one-validation-report/investigation.md`, capture part, C4).
- The prefix type lives in `domain::identity`. Unique, ambiguous and unresolved outcomes are asserted by the graph tests at `graph.rs:2702,2768,2877`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: Each graph evaluation builds one index over its resolution issues, and every container pointer resolves through it without normalising candidate ids.
- [hard] REQ-02: Unique, ambiguous and unresolved pointers resolve exactly as before, the minimum prefix length included; the existing graph tests pass unchanged.
- [hard] REQ-03: A graph unit test resolves pointers given in different case and hyphenation against one index and shows the unique, ambiguous and unresolved outcomes.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Graph evaluation resolves container-from-label pointers through one id index instead of normalising candidate ids per pointer.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One index replaces one linear resolver inside graph.rs.

title: Item links resolve against one address index with item kinds resolved once
description:
Make item-link validation resolve every qualified link against one address index value, and resolve the configured item kinds once per set of captured declarations.

## Background

- `collect_item_link_findings` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:697-843`) builds a set of canonical addresses from issue-embedded items and project sources (`:713-749`), then resolves each issue-scoped address by scanning every issue with a prefix (`:800-814`).
- Item kinds are resolved by `resolve_item_kinds` in that pass (`:703`) and again for every rendered projection inside the same validation (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/projection_render.rs:67`, reached from `repository_state/materialize.rs:319`).
- Captured declarations are parsed once into `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mod.rs:435-490`).
- Item kinds hold their id pattern as an `IdPattern`, kind scope is the domain `KindScope`, and item-address issue segments are `IssueIdPrefix` values.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: A domain address-index type holds the canonical addresses of every issue-embedded and project item and resolves an issue-scoped address's prefix in one lookup; repository validation builds it once per validation and resolves every link label against it.
- [hard] REQ-02: `CapturedRepositoryDeclarations` resolves the configured item kinds once, and item-link validation and projection rendering read them from there; neither calls `resolve_item_kinds`.
- [hard] REQ-03: Unit tests over the address index show a resolved project address, a resolved issue-scoped address given by short prefix, an alias-form address resolving like its canonical form, an ambiguous issue scope and a dangling address; the existing item-link tests pass unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour is unchanged. An invalid item-kind declaration still fails the effective-configuration pass with the same error.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: Repository validation resolves item links through one address index, and resolves item kinds once from the captured declarations.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One extracted index type and one kinds field reach two consumers.

title: One loader parses the index and issue records
description:
Parse `.jit/index.json` and every indexed issue record through one loader, and make repository validation, validation capture and mutation bases call it.

## Background

Three loaders parse the same records:

- `load_records` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:353-415`) parses the index with `RepositoryIndex::parse`, every indexed record, checks each record's embedded id, and reconciles the captured `.jit/issues` listing against the index.
- `effective_index_ids` and `effective_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:773-802`) parse the index through a private `IndexIds` struct and the records leniently, over overlay-effective bytes during capture.
- `captured_active_issues` (`crates/jit/src/commands/mod.rs:2062-2100`) parses both through `storage::json::parse_repository_index` and reports a missing record as issue-not-found; mutation bases, gate checking, archive and gate commands call it.

Kept as one change for a build reason: the three private loaders are replaced together, and an uncalled private function fails the zero-warning build.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: One function in `repository_state` parses the index and every indexed record from a byte source into parsed records (index ids and issues in index order), checking embedded ids and, where the listing was captured, reconciling it against the index; its errors are typed.
- [hard] REQ-02: `load_records`, `effective_index_ids`, `effective_issues`, the `IndexIds` struct and `captured_active_issues`' own parsing no longer exist; each former caller calls the loader.
- [hard] REQ-03: Each caller keeps its error contract: mutation captures report a missing indexed record as issue-not-found, and repository validation reports index, record and listing disagreements with today's messages.
- [hard] REQ-04: Unit tests own the loader's cases: a well-formed set, a missing record, a mismatched embedded id, an unparseable record and a listing that disagrees with the index.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: The index and issue records are parsed by one loader shared by validation, capture and mutation bases.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: Three private loaders converge on one new loader; deleting them makes the change one unit.

title: One pure function computes the validation report
description:
Replace the two repository-validation entry points and their `Result` pair with one pure function that computes a `ValidationReport` from a captured validation and the inputs its caller supplies.

## Background

- `validate_repository` (`crates/jit/src/validation/repository.rs:152-181`) derives the materialization plan and calls `validate_repository_with_materializations` (`:183-332`); both return `Result<RepositoryValidationReport, RepositoryValidationFailure>` (`:52-130`), where the failure carries the partial report.
- The function is not pure: `collect_rule_findings` reads the wall clock (`:589`), and `validate_machine_local_claims` (`:536-552`) reads `crate::test_mode` and calls `crate::commands::validate_claims_index_at` (`commands/validate.rs:2457-2463`), which re-detects the worktree layout and reads the machine-local claims index.
- Callers: `commands/validate.rs` (`validate_silent` `:107-125`, `validate_repository_report` `:523-532`, `validate_repository_report_with_divergences` `:535-545`, `capture_validation_report` `:547-586`, `capture_repair_plan` `:650-703`), `commands/gate_check.rs` (`repository_rule_report` `:435-443`, `gate_findings_from_report` `:634-660`, the repository checker at `:1045-1050`), `commands/init.rs:284-292,498-520,680`, `commands/profile.rs:26,358,1570`, `commands/config.rs:328`, `main.rs` (the whole-repository validate arm, about `:6805-6900`), the tests in `validation/repository.rs` and `crates/jit/tests/fast_rules/undeclared_taxonomy_tests.rs:183`.
- The validation layer parses records through the shared records loader.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `validation::report(&CapturedValidation, &ReportInputs) -> ValidationReport` is the only function that computes the repository report. `CapturedValidation` pairs a captured image with the records the loader parsed from it, and `CapturedValidation::from_image` parses them. `validate_repository`, `validate_repository_with_materializations`, `RepositoryValidationReport` and `RepositoryValidationFailure` no longer exist.
- [hard] REQ-02: The report reads only its arguments: the evaluation instant and the claims-index problems are fields of `ReportInputs`, supplied by the executor, which computes the claims problems from its own worktree paths and keeps today's test-mode skip. `crates/jit/src/validation/` reads no clock, environment or machine-local file and calls no `crate::commands` function.
- [hard] REQ-03: `ValidationReport` exposes the passes reached, the structural failure if any, and the findings projected to the wire `RuleReport`; a structural failure keeps every finding collected before it.
- [hard] REQ-04: Every listed caller computes the report through the new function, and `jit validate`, `config set`, `init`, profile apply and the repository-validation gate keep their output and exit status; the existing suites pass, and a unit test shows that an injected instant decides a `gate-recency` finding.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: A single pure validation-layer function computes the whole-repository report from a captured image and injected inputs.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The report type replaces a Result pair whose callers only compile together.

title: Validation capture hands its parsed records to the report

title: Validation views are selections of the report
description:
Give `ValidationReport` the provenance each finding needs and a selection operation, so every validation view can be computed as a filter of the one report.

## Background

- `ValidationReport` holds findings projected to the wire `ReportedFinding` (`crates/jit/src/validation/report.rs:23`), which keeps the attributed issue, rule, severity and message only. ## Background

- The `issue create` arm (`crates/jit/src/main.rs:2340-2440`) builds its JSON response through `get_dependencies_enriched` and `list_gate_runs` after the commit, and its human path lists every issue and calls `evaluate_graph_rules`, which captures a whole validation image, to print graph warnings; `--force` and `--quiet` suppress them, `--orphan` drops `orphan-leaf`. JSON output carries no findings. Measured on this repository: human 629 ms against 76 ms with `--quiet` (`dev/active/9876a23a-one-validation-report/investigation.md`, capture part, C6).
- A new issue has no dependencies and no gate runs, so its enriched dependencies and gate runs are empty by construction.
- The JSON payload type is `IssueShowResponse` (`crates/jit/src/output.rs`), registered for `issue create` in `crates/jit/src/schema.rs:542-548`; the MCP bridge generates its create tool from that schema. `ClaimResponse` (`output.rs:1341-1346`) flattens an issue beside `warnings`.
- `--orphan` tests: `tests/cli_issue/quiet_mode_tests.rs`, `tests/cli_query_graph/label_hierarchy_e2e_test.rs`, `tests/cli_query_graph/graph_json_tests.rs`; create-warning tests: `tests/fast_rules/cli_warnings_integration_tests.rs`.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `issue create --json` returns an `IssueCreateResponse` that flattens the issue view and adds `findings`, registered in the schema for `issue create`; the human path prints one line per finding. Both show the same findings, after `--orphan` drops `orphan-leaf`; `--force` suppresses none; `--quiet` keeps printing only the id.
- [hard] REQ-02: After creation publishes, the arm makes no storage, executor or capture call: no issue list, no graph-rule evaluation, no dependency enrichment and no gate-run listing.
- [hard] REQ-03: A CLI test creates an orphan leaf with `--json` and finds its `orphan-leaf` finding in `findings`, and with the human path finds the same finding; the JSON assertion fails on today's code, whose response has no `findings`.
- [hard] REQ-04: The create-warning tests read the CLI output or the returned findings, and the `--orphan` tests pass.

## Notes

- Behaviour change: JSON output gains `findings`; local-rule and graph-rule findings print together; `--force` no longer hides them.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: issue create shows the returned findings identically in human and JSON output with no read after the mutation commits.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One CLI arm, one response type and its schema registration change together.

title: One mutation and one post-fix report for validate --fix
description:
Make `jit validate --fix` derive every fix from one captured validation, publish them in one mutation, and always render the one report computed over the fixed repository.

## Background

- `validate_with_fix` (`crates/jit/src/commands/validate.rs:42-97`) first runs a full validation whose result fix mode discards (`:44`), then publishes each hierarchy type fix (`detect_and_fix_hierarchy_issues` `:1140-1216`, `apply_type_fix` `:1218-1234`, reading the hierarchy and issue list from disk), the transitive reduction (`reduce_all_dependencies`, already one mutation), each readiness correction in up to ten passes (`check_pending_transitions` `:2085-2141`, one lifecycle mutation per correction) and the derived-state repair (`repair_derived_state` `:599-643`, one mutation). It re-validates only when it applied a fix, so a zero-fix run over an index that disagrees with the issue files prints "No fixes needed" and exits 0 while plain `jit validate` fails.
- Pure derivations exist: `generate_fixes` over `detect_validation_issues` (`domain::type_taxonomy`), `derive_dependency_repair` (`crates/jit/src/commands/dependency.rs:854`, private), `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` (`domain/types.rs`), and `derive_materialization` for derived state. `finalize` (`crates/jit/src/repository_state/mutation.rs:719`) turns issue intents into a plan, and `RepositoryDelta::new` (`repository_state/image.rs:1239-1256`) accepts concatenated actions and refuses duplicate targets.
- The `--fix` arm of `main.rs` (about `:6754-6800`) renders `{valid, fixes_applied, dry_run, message}` in JSON. `jit recover` calls `repair_derived_state` (`commands/claim.rs:733`) and keeps doing so.

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: `--fix` computes no report before deriving its fixes. It derives the hierarchy, reduction, readiness and derived-state fixes from one validation capture, folding the issue edits per issue, and publishes them all through one mutation; `--dry-run` derives the same plan and publishes nothing.
- [hard] REQ-02: Readiness corrections apply `Issue::derive_readiness_correction` to the projected issue set until none remains; no other readiness derivation is introduced.
- [hard] REQ-03: `--fix` always computes one report over the repository as the fixes leave it, including when it applied none, and renders it as plain `jit validate` does, with the fix count and messages; its exit status follows that report. A harness test shows one publication carrying fixes of every class, and a CLI test over an index that disagrees with the issue files shows `--fix` failing as plain `validate` does, which fails on today's code.
- [hard] REQ-04: The listed fix suites pass with their assertions on repository state unchanged.

## Notes

- Behaviour and output change: `--fix --json` carries the post-fix report fields and its exit status follows that report.
- A later pure readiness derivation that every mutation shares will replace the fixpoint loop in this change.
- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: --fix derives its fixes from one capture, commits them in one mutation and always shows one post-fix report.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: The fix return value and its renderer compile only together, so one change carries both.

title: Measure validation views on this repository
description:
Measure the validation views and the side paths on a copy of this repository with a release build, and record the run as evidence.

## Background

- `scripts/benchmark-mutation-cost.sh` builds fixture copies of this repository (`git clone --shared` plus `.jit` sync), waits for a low load average, and times commands as the median of several runs; its committed run is `dev/benchmarks/publication-cost-722878d4/`.
- Before this work, `jit validate <id>` took about three times as long as whole-repository `jit validate` on this repository (`dev/active/9876a23a-one-validation-report/investigation.md`, capture part, REQ-08 row).

## Success Criteria

- [hard] REQ-01: The harness, generalised in `scripts/benchmark-mutation-cost.sh`, times `jit validate`, `jit validate <id>`, `jit validate --scope <container>`, `jit validate <id> --explain`, `jit issue create` (human, `--json`, `--quiet`) and `jit validate --fix --dry-run` on a fresh copy of this repository, load-gated, as medians.
- [hard] REQ-02: `dev/active/9876a23a-one-validation-report/benchmark/README.md` records one run with the commit, the release binary, the fixture's issue count, the host load before and after, and every median, with the raw timings beside it.
- [hard] REQ-03: In the recorded run the median of `jit validate <id>` is no greater than the median of whole-repository `jit validate`.

## Notes

- Written against the code as it stands after the changes this one follows; line citations name current code.

planning.outcome: A scripted release-build run on a copy of this repository records per-issue validation no slower than whole validation.

terminal.worker_sized_reason: One harness extension and one recorded run fit one cycle.
